units.claim: common is a cross-cutting layer of helpers and adapters usable by all other layers.

citations.quote: There's also another layer called "common" that you can use as a [cross-cutting concern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-cutting_concern) layer.

units.claim: domain holds the entities (models) and the use-case interfaces, and is the innermost business layer.

citations.quote: This is the "domain" or "entities" layer. Here's the description by Uncle Bob:

units.claim: application holds the use cases, their ports, validations and errors.

citations.quote: This is the **"Use Cases"** layer. Here you may add the application **Use cases**. Here's the description by Uncle Bob:

units.claim: presentation holds the controllers, middlewares and responses that adapt data between the use cases and the outside.

citations.quote: I'm using the name **"Presentation"** for this layer.

units.claim: infrastructure holds the express, knex and repository implementations, which are the outermost frameworks and drivers.

citations.quote: This folder (layer) is where we add everything related to external "**Frameworks and Drivers**". Here you can add the repositories, external frameworks, web and so on.

units.claim: main is the composition root where factories wire everything together, and it may depend on all layers.

citations.quote: This layer is where we put everything together. It's the "dirty layer", because most factories will be here. It may depend on all other layers in the system.

units.claim: Layers run from the innermost (common, domain) outward through application, presentation, infrastructure and main, and dependencies point inwards.

citations.quote: This rule says that source code dependencies can only point inwards.
In our case, data enter the system via "express routes" (infrastructure layer) to the "controllers" (adapters layer), to the "use cases" (application layer), to the "domain" (domain/entities layer).

units.claim: no-layer-skip is disabled because main may depend on every layer and the data flow crosses several layers.

citations.quote: This layer is where we put everything together. It's the "dirty layer", because most factories will be here. It may depend on all other layers in the system.

Knex seeds are data-loading scripts, not architectural code.
